summary: One script-driven sign-in panel at /login on the connection's own origin: an identifier field (mobile number or e-mail address), a password field and a button, with no form element around them. A cookie consent dialog covers the page on a first visit.

sources.title: The public My DIGI entry, rendered once without an account
sources.note: The entry address forwards to /login on the catalog host itself; no other host served the page. The sign-in controls are in the top document; the two other frames belong to the consent tool and hold no control.

sources.title: DIGI Portugal: legal notice and conditions of use of the website
sources.note: Clause 4.5: the access data of My DIGI are a password together with the mobile number given at registration or, for fibre-only customers, the e-mail address. Clause 3.4 forbids reproducing or copying the website's contents; it has no clause on automated access. No markup.

selectors.locator: frames[0], div#AuthLoginStep, div#AuthLoginStepButton, button.button-login (rendered, disabled while the fields are empty)

fixtures.note: In the capture the button is disabled until the fields have a value. The fixture has no script, so it leaves the disabled attribute out. The button's unusual type value, principal, is the page's own.

staysInteractive.note: A cookie consent dialog (div#CybotCookiebotDialog, overlay template) was displayed over the page in the capture. It is not answered by the steps.

unverified: The page can change at any time. This is one anonymous render on the review date; the generated class names seen in it are not used by any selector.
Nothing after the button was observed, because no account was used: whether a code by SMS or e-mail, or any other check, follows the password.
That the button becomes enabled when the application types into the two fields, and that a click on it signs in. The panel has no form element, so the page's script handles the button.
Whether the consent dialog has to be answered before the fields accept input.
neededFromUser: One sign-in with this layout, or the page that follows the password saved as "Webpage, Complete" if one is shown. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: Checked before the capture: robots.txt of mydigi.digi.pt disallows nothing, and the legal notice has no clause on automated access. The capture loaded the page once and sent no input.
